newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen top-heavy, may test downside in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen top-heavy, may test downside in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to remain top-heavy against the yen during Asian trading time on Thursday after a sharp drop overnight on weaker-than-expected U.S. economic data and market talk that a newsletter had stated that the U.S. Treasury was supporting a stronger yen.

Dealers said the dollar may test the downside again in Tokyo after falling as far as around 116.55 yen in Sydney, but this would depend on whether Japanese investors started selling dollars aggressively.
Short-covering by interbank dealers was also expected to emerge on dips.

In late trade in New York on Wednesday, the greenback was sold heavily for yen when a market rumour emerged that a newsletter from a Washington-based consulting firm had stated that U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin is calling for an exchange rate of 115 yen per dollar. Yet subscribers to the newsletter contacted by Reuters denied receiving such a report.

Also, a weaker-than-expected U.S. Producer Price Index, which fell 0.6 percent in April, the largest decline since August 1993, reduced expectations that the Fed will tighten credit at a Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday. This also became a bearish factor for the dollar.
